candidates.current_role: State Representative, Texas House District 110, since 2013
candidates.background: Rose represents District 110, which includes Oak Cliff, Pleasant Grove and Balch Springs in Dallas County. She is an alumna of Paul Quinn College and previously served on City of Dallas boards, including the Planning and Zoning Commission. In the 89th Legislature she was vice chair of the House Calendars Committee and served on Appropriations and Human Services, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Says her legislative focus is mental health, access to affordable health care and criminal justice reform.
Highlights state budget funding she secured for mental health authorities, early childhood intervention and school meal programs.

record.text: Authored HB 12, which extended postpartum Medicaid coverage for new mothers from two to 12 months, according to her official biography.

In 2025 authored HB 2402 (Medicaid fees and rates), HB 2809 (DFPS reporting on youth suicide attempts), HB 5155 (maternal opioid misuse model under Medicaid) and HB 5394, which became law, and HB 2777 to bar the death penalty for people with severe mental illness, which failed in committee.
Voted against SB 2 (2025), which created the state education savings account program, on third reading.
In 2023 voted for the April 2023 budget amendment barring state funds for vouchers and for the November 2023 amendment removing education savings accounts from HB 1.
Voted for HB 2 (2025 school finance) on third reading and voted to concur in the final Senate version.
Voted for a 2025 budget amendment (Amendment No. 22 to SB 1) directing the state to seek a federal waiver to expand Medicaid, which failed 63 to 85.
Voted against SB 10 (2025), requiring Ten Commandments displays in public school classrooms.
Voted for SJR 5 (the 2025 bail constitutional amendment) and voted against SB 9 (2025 bail procedures).
Voted against SB 3 (2025), which would have banned most hemp-derived THC products, on third reading.
In 2025 voted against SB 8 (requiring certain sheriffs to enter agreements with ICE) and SB 1362 (barring enforcement of extreme risk protective orders).
In the August 2025 second special session voted against HB 4 (2025 mid-decade congressional redistricting) and against HB 7 (2025, civil lawsuits over abortion-inducing drugs).

In 2023 voted against SB 14 (ban on gender transition treatments for minors), HB 2127 (state preemption of local regulations), SB 3 (state border barrier funding) and SB 4 (state illegal entry offense).
Voted for impeaching Attorney General Ken Paxton in May 2023.
Voted for Dustin Burrows over David Cook in the January 2025 runoff vote for Speaker of the House.
Was recorded absent on August 5, 2025, when the House lacked a quorum during the House Democrats' walkout over congressional redistricting.

notes.text: Ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary; no other candidate is listed for this seat in this guide's roster.
Named among Texas Monthly's Best Legislators in 2023, according to her official biography.
